tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.final:
**Payment reported:**

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Vendor | Evergreen Catering (V-519) |
| Invoice | INV-49004 |
| Amount | $2,969.92 (paid in full) |
| Rail | Wire from operating account |
| Payment ID | PAY0001 |
| Status | Sent → invoice marked **paid** |

Notes:
- Evergreen had three invoices on file. Only INV-49004 was in **approved** status, so that is the one I paid. INV-23798 was already paid previously, and INV-79479 is still a draft ("Awaiting approval") and was not touched.
- The vendor's bank details are verified, so wire was used as requested.
- The amount is below the $10,000 controller-approval threshold, so no additional approval was required.
- The wire went out on the first attempt only (single call, with an idempotency key), so it was paid exactly once. The tool did not automatically reconcile the payment to the invoice, so I linked PAY0001 to INV-49004, which is what flipped the invoice to "paid."
- One oddity worth flagging: `list_payments` still returns an empty list even though the wire was sent and the invoice shows paid with payment ID PAY0001. The payment record may not be surfacing in that reporting view — you may want the systems team to check that the wire appears in the operating-account payment ledger before month-end reconciliation.
